svc_helpdesk.lockout_policy: none - excluded from lockout to prevent service interruption
svc_helpdesk.intended_use: Unattended helpdesk automation. Not intended for interactive logon.

analyst_notes: Nine accounts, a handful of attempts each, spread over 36 minutes. That is password spraying - designed to stay under a lockout threshold.
The account that worked had a password set in 2019 and was explicitly excluded from the lockout policy.
Server Operators is a privileged group. This service account could do considerably more than raise tickets.
Logon type 10 means RemoteInteractive - somebody sitting at an RDP session, not an automated service.

content.change_justification: Temporary remote access for estates contractors during campus closure. To be removed when contractors finish (April 2021).
analyst_notes: A rule created as a temporary measure in 2021 and never removed. This is the single most common way an institution ends up with RDP on the internet.
Source is 'any'. Even keeping remote access, restricting it to the contractor's address range would have prevented this.
184,000 hits in thirty days on a rule nobody reviews. Most of that is the internet knocking.
This is student personal data. Whatever else this incident is, it is now a notifiable data breach and the institution's data protection officer needs to know tonight.
temp$ is a hidden administrative share - the dollar suffix keeps it out of network browsing. Staging there is a choice, not an accident.
The archive was created at 02:05 and the outbound transfer began at 02:31. Twenty-six minutes was all the warning anyone had.
